explanation: Young crows learn the craft partly by watching adults, and tool styles differ between areas of the island, a little like local traditions. They also cut barbed probes from leaf edges.

claims.text: New Caledonian crows make hooked tools from twigs and use them to extract insect larvae from holes.
Eurasian magpies, keel-billed toucans and keas are not known for making hooked tools.
Young New Caledonian crows learn tool-making partly by watching adults.
New Caledonian crow tool designs vary between regions of the island.
New Caledonian crows also make barbed probes from the edges of pandanus leaves.

evidence.restatement: New Caledonian crows make hooked tools from twigs and use them to pull larvae out of holes.
Eurasian magpies, keel-billed toucans and keas are not known for making hooked tools.
Young crows pick up tool-making partly by watching adults, although basic tool use appears even in hand-raised birds.
Pandanus tool designs differ between regions of New Caledonia (Hunt and Gray).
They also cut barbed, stepped probes from the edges of pandanus leaves.

issues.note: The explanation's 'Young crows learn the craft from adults' is a little stronger than c3: hand-raised juveniles develop basic tool use without adults, and watching adults refines it. 'learn partly from adults' would match the claim.
